newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco floods cause $13.6 mln damage to crops.
newsitem.headline: Morocco floods cause $13.6 mln damage to crops.

text.p: Floods and winter rains, which recently hit some 13,600 hectares of cereals and other agricultural crops in northern Morocco, caused damage estimated at $13.6 million, the Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday.
In a statement, the ministry said 11,970 hectares of cereals were damaged by floods in the Gharb region. Another 1,663 hectares of wheat and sugar crops were destroyed in Loukkos province.
"The total losses were estimated at 129 million dirhams," the ministry said.
Agriculture Minister Hassan Abouyoub visited both areas and announced measures to support farmers who suffered from the floods, it said.
Earlier this month, a Moroccan official told Reuters there would be no impact from the floods on the country's cereal imports.
Morocco plans to import 1.0 million tonnes of soft wheat in the 1996/97 season (July/June).
It harvested a record 10 million tonnes of cereals and a total of 76,800 hectares of sugar cane and beet in 1995/96, the Statistics Directorate said.
A Casablanca-based think-tank has forecast the country will produce 7.0 to 8.0 million tonnes of cereals in 1996/97 season.
A total of 5.6 million hectares are expected to be sown for all crops in the 1996/97 season, similar to 1995/96, an official said. Nearly 900,000 hectares are located in irrigated areas, he said.
More than 65 percent of the total area had been sown since October 1996, he added.
